submission.title: Verified resolution refutation checker for list-based CNFs
submission.claim: Defines an executable propositional resolution step (resolve on a pivot, appending the resolvent only when both premises are already derived) and a checker that accepts a step list iff it derives the empty clause from the input CNF. Proves soundness: whenever the checker accepts, every Boolean assignment falsifies the CNF. A second conjunct shows the checker is not vacuous: it accepts a three-step refutation of the complete two-variable CNF. This gives the repository its first machine-checked UNSAT certificate format, complementing the credited SAT-side locality result.
submission.novelty: First proof-system artifact in this ledger: earlier accepted work covers renaming, namespaces and assignment locality, all about satisfying assignments. This adds a checkable certificate of unsatisfiability. That is the coNP side, where Cook–Reckhow proof systems and resolution lower bounds such as Haken's live. Soundness of resolution and verified UNSAT checkers are well known; the contribution is a self-contained constructive Lean Core formalization in this pinned grammar, reusable as a base for later work (for example, unit propagation as derived resolution, size measures on refutations, or a formal pigeonhole statement). No complexity result is claimed.

prior_art.relationship: Origin of the resolution rule whose propositional soundness is formalized here.
Defines propositional proof systems as polynomial-time checkers; NP = coNP iff some system is polynomially bounded. This artifact is such a checker for resolution, with machine-checked soundness.
Exponential resolution lower bounds for pigeonhole formulas; a verified checker is the object such lower bounds quantify over.
Prior verified UNSAT certificate checker (Isabelle/HOL, GRAT) for a stronger proof format; this work is a small Lean Core analogue, not a new technique.
Prior verified checker for LPR proofs, which subsume resolution; no priority over verified certificate checking is claimed.

attribution.contributions: Definitions, statement and proof were written by an AI coding agent run by the PR author, then compiled with Lean 4.19.0 (axioms: propext, Quot.sound only) and the pinned grammar check. Disclosure: the PR author account is the repository operator account; the signing wallet is new and dedicated to this submission. No independent-contributor claim. No code from earlier submissions is reused.

submission.limitations: Soundness only: completeness of resolution (every unsatisfiable CNF has an accepted refutation) is not proved. Steps cite premise clauses by full content, so certificate size is not optimized and no running-time bound is proved. Resolvents are not deduplicated or checked for tautology. The non-vacuity witness is one small instance. Says nothing about lower bounds, NP versus coNP, or P versus NP.

evidence.proof:
{
  "version": 1,
  "definitions": [
    {
      "name": "evalLiteral",
      "type": "(Nat → Bool) → Nat × Bool → Bool",
      "value": "fun a l => a l.1 == l.2"
    },
    {
      "name": "evalClause",
      "type": "(Nat → Bool) → List (Nat × Bool) → Bool",
      "value": "fun a c => List.any c (evalLiteral a)"
    },
    {
      "name": "evalCNF",
      "type": "(Nat → Bool) → List (List (Nat × Bool)) → Bool",
      "value": "fun a f => List.all f (evalClause a)"
    },
    {
      "name": "resolve",
      "type": "Nat → List (Nat × Bool) → List (Nat × Bool) → List (Nat × Bool)",
      "value": "fun x c d => List.filter (fun l => decide (l ≠ (x, true))) c ++ List.filter (fun l => decide (l ≠ (x, false))) d"
    },
    {
      "name": "resolutionStep",
      "type": "Option (List (List (Nat × Bool))) → List (Nat × Bool) × List (Nat × Bool) × Nat → Option (List (List (Nat × Bool)))",
      "value": "fun st s => Option.bind st (fun cs => if s.1 ∈ cs ∧ s.2.1 ∈ cs then some (cs ++ [resolve s.2.2 s.1 s.2.1]) else none)"
    },
    {
      "name": "checkRefutation",
      "type": "List (List (Nat × Bool)) → List (List (Nat × Bool) × List (Nat × Bool) × Nat) → Bool",
      "value": "fun f steps => Option.any (fun cs => decide (([] : List (Nat × Bool)) ∈ cs)) (List.foldl resolutionStep (some f) steps)"
    }
  ],
  "statement": "(∀ (f : List (List (Nat × Bool))) (steps : List (List (Nat × Bool) × List (Nat × Bool) × Nat)), checkRefutation f steps = true → ∀ a : Nat → Bool, evalCNF a f = false) ∧ checkRefutation [[(0, true), (1, true)], [(0, true), (1, false)], [(0, false), (1, true)], [(0, false), (1, false)]] [([(0, true), (1, true)], [(0, true), (1, false)], 1), ([(0, false), (1, true)], [(0, false), (1, false)], 1), ([(0, true), (0, true)], [(0, false), (0, false)], 0)] = true",
  "proof": "by
  have rsound : ∀ (a : Nat → Bool) (x : Nat) (c d : List (Nat × Bool)), evalClause a c = true → evalClause a d = true → evalClause a (resolve x c d) = true := by
    intro a x c d hc hd
    obtain ⟨l, hl, hla⟩ := List.any_eq_true.mp hc
    obtain ⟨m, hm, hma⟩ := List.any_eq_true.mp hd
    apply List.any_eq_true.mpr
    cases hx : a x with
    | false =>
      have hne : l ≠ (x, true) := by
        intro h
        subst h
        simp [evalLiteral, hx] at hla
      exact ⟨l, List.mem_append_left _ (List.mem_filter.mpr ⟨hl, by simpa using hne⟩), hla⟩
    | true =>
      have hne : m ≠ (x, false) := by
        intro h
        subst h
        simp [evalLiteral, hx] at hma
      exact ⟨m, List.mem_append_right _ (List.mem_filter.mpr ⟨hm, by simpa using hne⟩), hma⟩
  have hnone : ∀ (r : List (List (Nat × Bool) × List (Nat × Bool) × Nat)), List.foldl resolutionStep none r = none := by
    intro r
    induction r with
    | nil => rfl
    | cons t rest2 ih2 => exact ih2
  have inv : ∀ (a : Nat → Bool) (steps : List (List (Nat × Bool) × List (Nat × Bool) × Nat)) (cs : List (List (Nat × Bool))), evalCNF a cs = true → ∀ (out : List (List (Nat × Bool))), List.foldl resolutionStep (some cs) steps = some out → evalCNF a out = true := by
    intro a steps
    induction steps with
    | nil =>
      intro cs hcs out hout
      simp at hout
      subst hout
      exact hcs
    | cons s rest ih =>
      intro cs hcs out hout
      rw [List.foldl_cons] at hout
      have hstep : resolutionStep (some cs) s = (if s.1 ∈ cs ∧ s.2.1 ∈ cs then some (cs ++ [resolve s.2.2 s.1 s.2.1]) else none) := rfl
      rw [hstep] at hout
      cases Decidable.em (s.1 ∈ cs ∧ s.2.1 ∈ cs) with
      | inl hmem =>
        rw [if_pos hmem] at hout
        have hall := List.all_eq_true.mp hcs
        have hnew : evalCNF a (cs ++ [resolve s.2.2 s.1 s.2.1]) = true := by
          apply List.all_eq_true.mpr
          intro c hc
          cases List.mem_append.mp hc with
          | inl hin => exact hall c hin
          | inr hin =>
            have hceq : c = resolve s.2.2 s.1 s.2.1 := List.mem_singleton.mp hin
            rw [hceq]
            exact rsound a s.2.2 s.1 s.2.1 (hall s.1 hmem.1) (hall s.2.1 hmem.2)
        exact ih (cs ++ [resolve s.2.2 s.1 s.2.1]) hnew out hout
      | inr hmem =>
        rw [if_neg hmem, hnone] at hout
        cases hout
  constructor
  · intro f steps hchk a
    cases hres : List.foldl resolutionStep (some f) steps with
    | none =>
      simp [checkRefutation, hres] at hchk
    | some out =>
      have hempty : ([] : List (Nat × Bool)) ∈ out := by
        simpa [checkRefutation, hres] using hchk
      cases hf : evalCNF a f with
      | false => rfl
      | true =>
        have hout := inv a steps f hf out hres
        have hc := (List.all_eq_true.mp hout) [] hempty
        simp [evalClause] at hc
  · decide
",
  "dependencies": []
}
